title: Reuse publication metadata: 15.7% less complete-check time (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Measured verifier improvement with a scoped acceptance-equivalence argument and finite controls; no new kappa. Reuse the committed SOURCES.json bytes already authenticated by the complete publication byte/history check.

```diff
 exact working/committed byte comparison and final reader-status check
- reread committed SOURCES.json through two extra Git processes
+ reuse its already compared immutable payload, bounded by 16 MiB
 unchanged metadata validation and raw source-pin ancestry checks
```

On the unchanged selected P104 package, median complete `check()` time falls from **120.33 ms to 101.49 ms**, a **15.66% reduction**. On a small stage-zero package it falls from 121.65 ms to 99.36 ms, an 18.33% reduction. Nine alternating runs per arm on each package have separated ranges and identical complete receipts; all 36 timed checks succeed. These are warm-process complete-function measurements on CPython 3.12.15/macOS arm64. Imports, baseline extraction and CLI startup are excluded from both arms. No scientific verifier is timed or audited.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit ywz65's byte preflight, Nick Petalas's earlier history check, roger-sato's immutable-source isolation, Douglas Colkitt's package runner and the retained reader contributors. The reuse technique is ordinary; the contribution is its bounded integration, failure controls and measured complete-check improvement. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19246957).

## Evidence

- Before: duplicate metadata reading accounts for about 21 ms in a separate 130 ms profile, dominated by synchronous Git operations. For the measured one-pin packages the change removes two of nine Git processes.
- After: **42 tests pass normally and under optimized Python**, with no skips. The final registered commands take 9.78 s and 10.02 s against 120 s limits. Complete hash-bound receipts agree. Controls cover byte drift, malformed committed metadata, final-reader failure ordering, exact size bounds, older refs, cross-call invalidation, unavailable/noncommit/side-branch pins, shallow history, replacements, grafts, modes and Git errors/timeouts.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, committed bytes, executable modes and declared source-history checks pass. The publication preflight checks 16 files at 60219737c80280a0bab577fe80f10b8c7b4fa22b.
- Official export and all nine declared input declarations pass. The exported-tree verifier also passes all 42 tests outside the project checkout, without project Git metadata. Git remains available for synthetic test fixtures.
- Static inspection confirms that the extracted metadata/history validator's AST is unchanged. Strict-warning syntax/control checks pass. No additional linter is installed locally.

From the worktree root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/publication-metadata-reuse/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/publication-metadata-reuse/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/publication-metadata-reuse
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/publication-metadata-reuse --check-source-history --check-modes
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/publication-metadata-reuse/benchmark.py --scratch /absolute/external/scratch --repeats 9
```

Elsewhere substitute CPython 3.12. The optional benchmark needs full history, an existing external scratch directory, both named benchmark packages and their VERIFY.json inputs materialized first. It obtains the original checker from canonical base `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419` and emits every sample, complete receipt and implementation hash. The generated original measurement receipt is retained below.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The stable-checkout contract remains required. At most 16 MiB of committed metadata remains live for one check; the existing full-blob reader allocation is unchanged. The standalone `source_history()` boundary still fetches its own committed metadata. The two removed Git operations no longer have failure events; errors from retained operations still propagate. The proof assumes successful immutable object reads, rather than identical subprocess traces.

No second-host performance, native Windows mode execution, selected scientific cold replay, physical multiplier, supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The five selected framework assumptions remain.

## Open next questions

Measure the same complete-check workload on a second operating system and Git implementation, retaining complete receipts and alternating samples. A second host and matching materialized inputs are required. No combined speedup with separate preflight optimizations is claimed.

## Related open work

- [#6155](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6155) removes eager mismatch-only SHA256 work in the same `check()` function in `scripts/check_research_commit.py`. Its comparison hunk around lines 130–139 overlaps this PR's hunk around 134–144. **Whichever lands second will likely need a merge-conflict resolution.** The mechanisms affect different cost stages; fixtures and timed boundaries differ, so their percentages are not compared or combined.
- [#6156](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6156) bounds working-source comparison memory in `scripts/research_package.py`. It changes another shared verifier script under the same `replay-runtime` card; this PR retains that module and claims no combined memory or timing benefit.
- [#6161](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6161) adds a numeric-reference prefilter in `scripts/find_overlap.py`, also under `replay-runtime`. It measures overlap search rather than publication checking. No common performance number is compared or combined.
- [#6164](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6164) supplies an opt-in adapter that batches source-commit resolution and ancestry queries. This PR removes duplicate committed-metadata reads while retaining those queries. No composed speedup is claimed.

The completion refresh checked this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM. The related shared-verifier submissions are listed above. No additional computations were run to compare their results.

## CI notes

**Uncertified by CI** at head `60219737c80280a0bab577fe80f10b8c7b4fa22b`. In [run 40726988089](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40726988089), [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40726988089/job/122952798845) was cancelled after reaching the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 10` limit. Its recorded lifetime is 16:32:40–16:42:42 UTC on October 28, 2026. The [package replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40726988089/job/122958625285) was skipped and **did not run in CI**.

The job metadata and log locate the cancellation in `actions/checkout` during the repository fetch. `Onboarding helper tests` is marked **skipped**, not failed. Thus this run does not show whether the edits to `scripts/check_research_commit.py` pass CI's onboarding tests. No claim that this change introduced no onboarding failure follows from this cancelled run. The checkout timeout is independent of the checker implementation.

Separately, canonical main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, the PR6030 kappa-admission commit pushed with `[skip ci]`, changed the selected record without updating its documentation contracts. Even without the timeout, the unchanged main baseline would fail these two onboarding tests:

- `test_research_current_status.CurrentStatusTests.test_current_section_matches_selected_record` expects standalone `**0.003125804**` in `docs/research/current-status.md`; the document instead bolds `0.003125804 = 781451/250000000` as one expression.
- `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` expects `make frontier6030-verify`; the actual test reads `docs/ci-verification.md`, whose current CI section still names #5599 and `make frontier5599-verify`.

Both [PR #6150 run 40724809789](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40724809789) and [PR #6120 run 40691776027](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691776027) report exactly those two failing tests. Their logs were read; they are separate evidence, not results of this PR's cancelled onboarding step. Open [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) targets the documentation fix.

**A maintainer re-run is needed after main is fixed.** This hosted run certified none of the package checks. The 42 normal/optimized local controls, registered replay, committed-byte/mode/source-history checks and exported replay remain separate passing local evidence. No push, CI re-run or main-document edit was made after this cancellation.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** publication-checker. The production diff retains one bounded immutable payload and extracts the unchanged history validator. Byte-only checking and standalone history checking retain their interfaces. Predecessor source pins and the selected frontier are unchanged.
